exposure: Planned mode of birth (caesarean section vs. vaginal birth)
cohort: 2,570 women with twin pregnancies from 25 countries who participated in the Twin Birth Study
finding: There were no clinically important differences in maternal outcomes at 3 months postpartum between women randomised to planned caesarean section compared with planned vaginal birth for twin pregnancies.
mod_finding: For women with twin pregnancies, the mode of birth was not associated with problematic urinary incontinence or urinary incontinence that affected the quality of life.
